currentContext.strengths: Leading position supplying yarn and fabrics to over 1,500 buyers in the Tirupur market, a major knitwear hub for the export of cotton apparels|Proven track record of execution, scale and efficiency, with garmenting as the growth engine supported by timely capacity additions and efficient utilisation levels|Captive renewable energy generation (including improved wind power generation) that has reduced power cost|High quality consciousness and timely commitment cited as retaining a reputed and leading customer base|Diversification through six wholly-owned subsidiaries spanning sugar, ethanol and co-generation alongside the textile business|Auditors' Report and Secretarial Audit Report for FY 2025-26 carry no qualification, reservation or adverse remark
currentContext.strategies: Run an integrated business model spanning spinning, knitting, processing, garmenting and co-generation, which management says provides resilience through changing manufacturing scenarios|Adopt advanced technologies and invest in modern infrastructure - continuing to upgrade spinning and manufacturing capabilities and to invest in next-generation technologies|Improve efficiency through process innovation wherever required|Strategic capacity expansion to capitalise on the expected revival of the textile sector|Expand the renewable energy footprint, especially solar power, as part of the green energy initiative, with a stated commitment to achieving 100% renewable energy for production processes|Focus on value-added products|Invest in the workforce through higher education, skill development and career progression, and sustain high women participation in the workforce|Investments of surplus funds are made only with the approval of the Board of Directors and primarily comprise investments in equity instruments of an unlisted entity and mutual funds, from which the Company does not expect significant credit risk. Ultimate responsibility for liquidity risk management rests with the Board, which has established a framework covering short-, medium- and long-term funding, managing liquidity by maintaining adequate reserves, banking facilities and reserve borrowing facilities and by matching the maturity profiles of financial assets and liabilities. Declaration of dividend on equity shares is placed before the members as ordinary business at the Annual General Meeting. Form AOC-2 records that there were no contracts or transactions not at arm's length and no material contracts at arm's length during the year.|35 MW solar plant installation completed across all units|Coal phase-out project started, using gas and biomass instead of coal, with a multi-fuel boiler set-up installed with ESP to control air pollution|Renewable energy through wind, co-generation and now solar caters to most of the Company's power requirements; captive renewable generation has reduced power cost and wind power generation improved during the year|Power-saving measures at production facilities: 5-star rated equipment, BLDC and IE3 motors, separate meters for monitoring, automated cutoff for boiler and compressor, and an energy audit before purchase of new equipment|Water management: fully automated control systems, flow meters, ETP and STP for recycling, ETP water used only in the processing unit, STP water used in green development areas to recharge ground water, and bore (ground) water no longer used for the production process|Chemical management: REACH-ECHA compliance, zero discharge of hazardous chemicals, Bhive tool to monitor chemical inventory and a fully automated set-up for dispensing dyes and chemicals|Sustainable cotton sourcing - BCI, Organic, CMIA and PSCP cotton bought as required, alongside Shankar-6 cotton from Gujarat for consistent quality|CSR contribution of Rs.1,598.73 Lakhs during the year, being 2.06% of the average three years' net profit of the Company, with the CSR policy published on the Company website|Grievance mechanisms for employees and workers run through an external NGO-monitored advisory body via 'Ungal Kural' and the 'Ulula' grievance system (toll-free number and app), plus the customer-brand-run 'TELL US' mechanism monitored by Primark; a Whistle Blower Policy is in place and published|BRSR disclosures are made on a standalone basis and no external assurance provider was engaged for the report
currentContext.expansion: Expansion in FY 2025-26 was led by modernization rather than by a named new project. Under the modernization programs old cards and knitted machines were replaced with new advanced machinery, and modernization in the spinning and knitting divisions is still under way; alongside technological advancement throughout the value chain, the best possible automation is being established, which management says will result in economising the labour cost. Garmenting is described as the growth engine, supported by timely capacity additions and efficient utilization levels. Looking ahead, a large scale green field garment expansion is 'on the cards', with no capacity, cost or commissioning timeline disclosed. The Chairman frames the forward plan as strategic capacity expansion plus continued investment in technology and modernization. On the energy side, KPR continues to expand its renewable energy footprint especially solar power, with a stated commitment to achieving 100% renewable energy for production processes; captive renewable generation has reduced power cost and wind power generation improved during the year. In the subsidiaries, sugarcane crushing commenced in November 2025 at both K.P.R. Sugar Mill Limited and KPR Sugar and Apparels Limited, each operating a co-generation plant whose output is partly sold and partly captively consumed, with ethanol produced from sugar syrup and molasses entirely for Oil Marketing Companies. No rupee capex figure, plant location list or project timetable is disclosed in the routed sections.
currentContext.mdna: Free Trade Agreements with major economies giving India tariff parity with competing countries are expected to propel the textile sector forward|Revival in demand and supportive policies are expected to propel the textile sector forward|India's resilience supported by strong domestic consumption, focused government initiatives in manufacturing and infrastructure and a stable macroeconomic environment, with the outlook described as positive|Global environment marked by trade tensions, policy fluctuations and tariff pressures that have strained supply chains, increased costs and delayed investment decisions across industries|KPR's positioning to capitalise on the opportunity rests on strategic capacity expansion, continued investment in technology and modernization, strengthening of green energy initiatives and focus on value-added products

risks.risk: Cotton price volatility and availability of high-quality cotton
risks.note: BRSR flags sustainable raw material procurement as both opportunity and risk: 'Cotton being our key raw material, sourcing of high quality cotton at competitive price is always a major challenge. Speculative trading, unseasonal rains and global shortage are the causes of its price fluctuations.' Cotton is described as a single major cost of production, so price fluctuation directly hits the bottom line. Mitigation is a dedicated cotton team and exclusive personnel stationed in cotton growing areas, with quality cotton (Shankar-6 from Gujarat) sourced for consistency.

Exports contributed 38.42% of turnover in the reporting year and apparels are sold to leading brands from more than 60 countries, so demand, tariff and trade-policy shifts in overseas markets flow straight through to the business. Domestic yarn and fabric sales are themselves concentrated in the Tirupur market.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption and energy cost inflation
risks.note: Management notes that although the India-US and India-EU trade agreements materially improve India's tariff competitiveness, 'the sudden escalation of conflict in the Middle East has once again disrupted this momentum. For India, the impact is immediate particularly in the form of rising energy costs and supply uncertainties.'

risks.risk: Handling of hazardous and toxic chemicals in processing
risks.note: BRSR lists chemical management as an opportunity and a risk: cautious and efficient handling of hazardous and toxic chemicals is required in production. Mitigation is worker training by industry experts, a safe chemical disposal mechanism, REACH-ECHA compliance, zero discharge of hazardous chemicals and a fully automated dye and chemical dispensing set-up.

risks.risk: Water dependence of the processing operations
risks.note: Water is treated as a vital resource for the processing units; the Company has stopped using bore (ground) water for the production process and relies on fully automated controls, flow meters and ETP/STP recycling, with ETP water used only in the processing unit and STP water used to recharge ground level water in green development areas.

risks.risk: Energy sourcing and coal phase-out transition
risks.note: Power is a significant input; the Company relies on wind, co-generation and now solar for most of its power requirement and has started a coal phase-out project substituting gas and biomass, with a multi-fuel boiler and ESP installed for air pollution control. Execution of this transition and the cost of purchased power drive the cost of production.

risks.risk: Cyclicality and policy dependence of the sugar and ethanol businesses (subsidiaries)
risks.note: The sugar industry is described as historically agro-based and cyclical, with profitability now determined by ethanol blending, power co-generation and by-products. Ethanol demand rests on government blending policy - India reportedly targeted 30% ethanol blending with petrol by 2030 - and management observes that 'In India the capacity is ready; the technology is in place - What the industry needs now is certainty to plan the future with confidence.'

The workforce is large and predominantly female at worker level, and management is establishing the best possible automation throughout the value chain expressly to economise labour cost, indicating labour cost as a structural pressure on the cost base.

one-line thesis: KPR Mill leverages its fully integrated textile value chain and renewable energy capabilities to maintain profitability amid industry-wide margin pressures, while strategically expanding garment capacity and exploring FASO retail growth; sugar-ethanol segment provides stable cash flow with potential upside from policy-driven production shifts.
financial scorecard: rev: +25% YoY; EBITDA: -8% YoY; PAT: -5% YoY; orderbook: INR 1,000+ Cr; netdebt: negative (net cash)
guidance: Brownfield garment expansion to complete H1FY25, increasing capacity to 177M pcs; no overseas expansion planned; sugar-ethanol production to normalize in FY25 with higher sugar output; FASO targeting INR 100 Cr revenue in 3 years; no new capex beyond current plans until market improves.
segment / subsidiary detail: Yarn: 19,000 tons, INR 496 Cr, 12% margin; Fabric: 2,285 tons, INR 66 Cr; Garments: 40M pcs/quarter, INR 170/pc realization, 22-24% margin; Sugar: 176K tons FY24, INR 73 Cr/quarter; Ethanol: 9 Cr litres FY24, INR 150 Cr/quarter; Combined sugar-ethanol margin: 28%; FASO: INR 25 Cr/year (South India only)
growth verticals / optionality: UK FTA could unlock 5-10% additional export market share; FASO retail expansion to INR 100 Cr in 3 years; potential for further brownfield garment capacity if demand sustains; ethanol production scaling with policy support.
margins & cost dynamics: Yarn margin down to 12% (from 15%) due to cotton price volatility and oversupply; garment margin stable at 22-24% due to value addition (printing, embroidery); sugar-ethanol margin 28% driven by ethanol mix; energy cost pressure offset by 100% captive renewable power (solar + wind + co-gen).
capex / expansion: INR 30M garment capacity expansion (brownfield) to complete H1FY25; no new greenfield capex planned; no ethanol/sugar capex announced; total FY24 capex not disclosed but implied low due to net cash position.
capital allocation: Dividend increased; no buyback announced; net cash position allows flexibility; capital allocation contingent on market recovery; potential for FASO investment or textile capex if demand improves.
risks & watch-items: Persistent yarn margin pressure due to oversupply and competition from China/Vietnam/Bangladesh; weak global demand in Europe/US; UK FTA not guaranteed; sugar inventory delays due to government quotas; FASO retail may require sustained cash burn; cotton price volatility.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges industry headwinds but highlights resilience through integration and value addition; focused on domestic expansion; avoids overpromising on overseas or new capex; emphasizes patience until market recovers.
non-obvious takeaways: Despite low EBITDA margins, KPR maintains PAT stability via captive renewable energy (32 Cr units co-gen, 12 Cr consumed internally), reducing energy cost volatility; FASO retail is a low-cost dealer-model play with minimal capex; sugar inventory of 150K tons implies future revenue visibility once quotas release.

themes.title: Bioenergy / Ethanol / SAF transition
themes.need: Higher ethanol-blending mandates (E20->E25/E27/E30), CBG, SAF and bio-IBA underpin a multi-year bioenergy capex cycle. PRAJIND's near-term earnings are depressed by a 1G slowdown + GenX gestation but the optionality (SAF, CBG, DC-cooling) is large; TRUALT/BALRAMCHIN/EIDPARRY/TRIVENI/GODAVARIB add ethanol/sugar; BCLIND/GULPOLY/GLOBUSSPR on grain-based distillation.
themes.driver: Higher blending-mandate notifications; SAF/CBG order conversion; sugar-cycle realisations.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

hero.oneLiner: K.P.R. Mill Limited is a Coimbatore-based textile manufacturer of yarn, fabric and garments and a leading supplier of yarn and fabrics to over 1,500 buyers in the Tirupur knitwear hub, with sugar, ethanol and co-generation businesses held through wholly-owned subsidiaries.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: K.P.R. Mill Limited is a Coimbatore-based textile manufacturer of yarn, fabric and garments and a leading supplier of yarn and fabrics to over 1,500 buyers in the Tirupur knitwear hub, with sugar, ethanol and co-generation businesses held through wholly-owned subsidiaries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: K.P.R. Mill Limited manufactures yarn, fabric and garments; garments and yarn each account for a little over 42% of turnover and fabric for the balance of the disclosed 90%. It supplies yarn and fabrics to over 1,500 regular domestic clients in the Tirupur market, a major knitwear hub for the export of cotton apparels, and supplies apparels to leading brands from more than 60 countries, with exports contributing 38.42% of turnover in the reporting year. Through six wholly-owned subsidiaries the group also crushes sugarcane and produces sugar, ethanol for Oil Marketing Companies and co-generated power, part of which is captively consumed.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Yarn: 19,000 tons, INR 496 Cr, 12% margin; Fabric: 2,285 tons, INR 66 Cr; Garments: 40M pcs/quarter, INR 170/pc realization, 22-24% margin; Sugar: 176K tons FY24, INR 73 Cr/quarter; Ethanol: 9 Cr litres FY24, INR 150 Cr/quarter; Combined sugar-ethanol margin: 28%; FASO: INR 25 Cr/year (South India only)

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Textiles:** Yarn, Fabric, Garment
- **Sugar and allied (through subsidiaries):** Sugar, Ethanol, Co-generated power

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic yarn and fabric buyers - over 1,500 regular domestic clients, concentrated in the Tirupur knitwear market
- Export apparel market - leading brands from more than 60 countries; exports were 38.42% of turnover in the reporting year
- Oil Marketing Companies - entire ethanol production of K.P.R. Sugar Mill Limited was meant for OMCs
- Power sold from subsidiary co-generation plants, with the balance captively consumed

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Brownfield garment expansion to complete H1FY25, increasing capacity to 177M pcs; no overseas expansion planned; sugar-ethanol production to normalize in FY25 with higher sugar output; FASO targeting INR 100 Cr revenue in 3 years; no new capex beyond current plans until market improves.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: UK FTA could unlock 5-10% additional export market share; FASO retail expansion to INR 100 Cr in 3 years; potential for further brownfield garment capacity if demand sustains; ethanol production scaling with policy support.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Free Trade Agreements with major economies giving India tariff parity with competing countries are expected to propel the textile sector forward
- Revival in demand and supportive policies are expected to propel the textile sector forward
- India's resilience supported by strong domestic consumption, focused government initiatives in manufacturing and infrastructure and a stable macroeconomic environment, with the outlook described as positive
- Global environment marked by trade tensions, policy fluctuations and tariff pressures that have strained supply chains, increased costs and delayed investment decisions across industries
- KPR's positioning to capitalise on the opportunity rests on strategic capacity expansion, continued investment in technology and modernization, strengthening of green energy initiatives and focus on value-added products

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Yarn margin down to 12% (from 15%) due to cotton price volatility and oversupply; garment margin stable at 22-24% due to value addition (printing, embroidery); sugar-ethanol margin 28% driven by ethanol mix; energy cost pressure offset by 100% captive renewable power (solar + wind + co-gen).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend increased; no buyback announced; net cash position allows flexibility; capital allocation contingent on market recovery; potential for FASO investment or textile capex if demand improves.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Expansion in FY 2025-26 was led by modernization rather than by a named new project. Under the modernization programs old cards and knitted machines were replaced with new advanced machinery, and modernization in the spinning and knitting divisions is still under way; alongside technological advancement throughout the value chain, the best possible automation is being established, which management says will result in economising the labour cost. Garmenting is described as the growth engine, supported by timely capacity additions and efficient utilization levels. Looking ahead, a large scale green field garment expansion is 'on the cards', with no capacity, cost or commissioning timeline disclosed. The Chairman frames the forward plan as strategic capacity expansion plus continued investment in technology and modernization. On the energy side, KPR continues to expand its renewable energy footprint especially solar power, with a stated commitment to achieving 100% renewable energy for production processes; captive renewable generation has reduced power cost and wind power generation improved during the year. In the subsidiaries, sugarcane crushing commenced in November 2025 at both K.P.R. Sugar Mill Limited and KPR Sugar and Apparels Limited, each operating a co-generation plant whose output is partly sold and partly captively consumed, with ethanol produced from sugar syrup and molasses entirely for Oil Marketing Companies. No rupee capex figure, plant location list or project timetable is disclosed in the routed sections.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges industry headwinds but highlights resilience through integration and value addition; focused on domestic expansion; avoids overpromising on overseas or new capex; emphasizes patience until market recovers.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "The Board reports no significant or material order passed by Regulators, Courts or Tribunals impacting the going concern status or future operations, no pendency of any proceeding under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, and no instance of one-time settlement with any bank or financial institution. Form AOC-2 reports Nil contracts or transactions not at arm's length and Nil material contracts at arm's length. Cases pending for more than ninety days under the reported complaints head were Nil.", "as_of": "2026-06-27"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Leading position supplying yarn and fabrics to over 1,500 buyers in the Tirupur market, a major knitwear hub for the export of cotton apparels
- Proven track record of execution, scale and efficiency, with garmenting as the growth engine supported by timely capacity additions and efficient utilisation levels
- Captive renewable energy generation (including improved wind power generation) that has reduced power cost
- High quality consciousness and timely commitment cited as retaining a reputed and leading customer base
- Diversification through six wholly-owned subsidiaries spanning sugar, ethanol and co-generation alongside the textile business
- Auditors' Report and Secretarial Audit Report for FY 2025-26 carry no qualification, reservation or adverse remark

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Persistent yarn margin pressure due to oversupply and competition from China/Vietnam/Bangladesh; weak global demand in Europe/US; UK FTA not guaranteed; sugar inventory delays due to government quotas; FASO retail may require sustained cash burn; cotton price volatility.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Despite low EBITDA margins, KPR maintains PAT stability via captive renewable energy (32 Cr units co-gen, 12 Cr consumed internally), reducing energy cost volatility; FASO retail is a low-cost dealer-model play with minimal capex; sugar inventory of 150K tons implies future revenue visibility once quotas release.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Run an integrated business model spanning spinning, knitting, processing, garmenting and co-generation, which management says provides resilience through changing manufacturing scenarios
- Adopt advanced technologies and invest in modern infrastructure - continuing to upgrade spinning and manufacturing capabilities and to invest in next-generation technologies
- Improve efficiency through process innovation wherever required
- Strategic capacity expansion to capitalise on the expected revival of the textile sector
- Expand the renewable energy footprint, especially solar power, as part of the green …
